definition: Deepfake pornography is generative AI pornography created by altering existing photographs or videos, using deepfake technology, to modify the appearance of the depicted individuals, typically without consent.
details: Deepfake pornography is controversial and has been the subject of lawsuits and criminal investigations because users create and distribute realistic photos and videos of non-consenting individuals, sometimes including minors. It has been used for revenge porn. Many countries have criminalized deepfake pornography through legislative measures and technological solutions.

explainer.lead: Deepfake pornography uses AI to alter real photos or videos so someone appears in pornographic imagery, typically without their consent. Because the results can look realistic, their creation and spread can cause serious harm and have led to lawsuits, criminal investigations, and new laws.

tiers.eli5: Imagine someone changing an ordinary picture of you into a made-up rude picture and showing it to others as though it were real. Deepfake pornography is the computer-made version of that trick, and it can hurt people even though the pictured event never happened.
tiers.practitioner: Engineering work in this area is primarily defensive, using technological measures to address non-consensual altered imagery and its distribution. Consent, believable outputs, and cases involving minors are central risks, while legal duties may differ across countries.
tiers.paperLevel: Deepfake pornography = pornographic media generated by applying deepfake technology to existing photographs or videos to modify the appearance of depicted individuals, typically without consent. Documented concerns include realistic non-consensual imagery, distribution, revenge porn, and involvement of minors; responses include legislation, criminal investigation, litigation, and technological measures.

explainer.example: A person alters an ordinary photograph of a former partner to create a realistic pornographic image, then shares it without permission. This can constitute revenge porn even though the original photograph was not pornographic and the depicted event never occurred.

usedIn.name: Revenge porn
usedIn.detail: Altered intimate-looking imagery is created or distributed to harm a person without consent.

usedIn.name: Non-consensual harassment
usedIn.detail: Realistic altered photos or videos can target people who never agreed to be depicted.

usedIn.name: Legal investigations
usedIn.detail: Creation and distribution have become subjects of lawsuits and criminal investigations.

explainer.intuition: The core idea is to turn existing visual material into pornographic imagery that falsely appears to depict a real person. The apparent realism is what makes non-consensual creation and distribution especially damaging.
howItWorks: Existing photographs or videos provide the source material.
Deepfake technology alters the appearance of the people depicted.
The result is pornographic imagery that can look realistic.
The imagery may then be distributed without the depicted person's consent.
explainer.whyItMatters: People can be depicted realistically without consent, and those depicted may sometimes be minors. These harms have prompted lawsuits, criminal investigations, legislation in many countries, and technological responses.
misconceptions: A realistic result does not mean it records a real event.
The source material need not originally be pornographic.
The harm is not limited to adults; minors are sometimes depicted.
